MATERIAL FINDING 1 (durable state-integrity / stamp publication): a custody operation nested in an enclosing registry transaction can publish a campaign freshness stamp for a registry revision that subsequently rolls back; reuse of that revision number lets a stale copy overwrite newer committed progress.

Authority: parent acceptance says a behind-head restored/forked copy can never sync/release over the newer head; repair design .8.3 explicitly requires campaign stamp writes to follow the registry commit. ADR 0012:129-130 says "a stale campaign database can never revert the timeline"; ADR 0020 section 3 retains persistence/rollback/identity integrity. SRD page/quote: not applicable; this is Eshyra custody/persistence authority, not an SRD mechanics claim.

However, syncBackCharacterFromCampaign at characterCustody.ts:448-457 and release at :552-573 stamp the separate campaign DB immediately after their INNER atomically returns. The same assumption is present at checkout :180-189, acquire :822-869, and catch-up :923-931. That is after SAVEPOINT RELEASE, not necessarily after the registry COMMIT. The future/phantom synced number is accepted as fresh by isRestoredBehindHead at :382-385 (synced >= head).
